data.summary: The extraction is broadly aligned with the plan tiers and many major benefit limits, but there are actionable issues: some schema-required fields are left null despite clear PDS content, some extracted fields omit important conditions, product names include tier names contrary to the field definition, and several source evidence entries are summaries rather than exact quotes/table cells. Some issues are affected by inconsistencies in the PDS parse, especially COVID and travel-delay wording.

findings.reason: The Ultimate plan has a specific legal-cost benefit for detention, but legal_expenses_limit is null. The field definition explicitly includes wrongful detention/arrest or similar legal-cost cover separate from liability defence.
findings.source_quote: Personal legal costs as a result of being detained

findings.reason: The Ultimate Plus plan has the same specific detention legal-cost benefit, but legal_expenses_limit is null.
findings.source_quote: Personal legal costs as a result of being detained

findings.reason: The PDS states that luggage item limits can be increased by paying an additional premium. This optional high-value item cover appears available generally, but optional_add_ons is null for this record; the same omission appears in other records except for a different Ultimate package.
findings.source_quote: may increase the item limit by paying an extra amount

findings.reason: The record includes the Optional Extra Benefits Package but omits the separate optional increase to luggage item limits, which the PDS says can be purchased by paying an additional premium.

findings.reason: The extracted standard excess description omits Section 5 Travel delay. Page 19 states the $60 excess applies to Sections 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, and Section 39 where relevant. This omission appears repeated across plan records.
findings.extracted_value: Standard excess: $60 per event on Sections 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and Section 39 where relevant. Age 75+ excess: $5,000 per claim for Sections 1 and 4. Additional excesses may apply for approved existing medical condition cover and will be advised in writing.

findings.reason: The extracted travel delay sub-limit says up to $200 after 6 hours and $200 each further 24 hours, matching the benefits table, but the policy wording states up to $300. This inconsistency is material and is not flagged in the extraction; it affects all plan records' travel_delay_limit wording.
findings.source_quote: up to $300 for reasonable additional hotel accommodation
findings.extracted_value: $1,000 (includes up to $200 after 6 hours and $200 each further 24 hours)

findings.reason: general_exclusions is null despite the PDS containing a dedicated general exclusions section with exclusions applicable to all sections. This omission appears across all product records.
findings.source_quote: Unless otherwise indicated these exclusions on pages 41-42 apply to all Sections

findings.reason: benefit_exclusions is null despite multiple benefit sections containing section-specific 'We will not pay for' exclusions. This omission appears across all product records.

The product_name includes the plan tier 'Essentials'. The canonical definition says product_name should be the product or PDS family excluding the individual plan tier where possible; the tier is already captured in plan_name. The same pattern appears for the other plan records.
findings.source_quote: The Cover-More Corporate Travel Insurance policy

findings.reason: Several source_evidence entries are not exact quotes or table cells but constructed summaries such as benefit-table descriptions. The canonical definition requires exact quotes or table cells, treating tables as first-class evidence.
